extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, classification staff, patent information professionals, and patent office trainers (esp. USPTO/EPO/KIPO/SIPO/other IPOs)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and implementation guidance for the Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) system at the USPTO, including CPC products, training, transition timeline, and where biotechnology inventions are classified. Includes examples of relevant CPC subclasses and groups for biotechnology.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Chronology of key CPC development and implementation events (e.g., October 2010 agreement to develop CPC; October 2012 CPC scheme made public; January 2013 launch of CPC; March 2013 first US patent applications published with CPC symbols; April 2013 first revised version; May 2013 first US patent grant with CPC symbols; August 2013 CPC Definitions available on the Internet; January 2014 and January 2015 stages of USPTO examiner transition; April 2015 USPTO stops publishing USPC on US patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the milestone dates to track adoption and transition steps. The timeline establishes when CPC became the classification system of record at the USPTO and when CPC symbols began appearing on U.S. patent publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC Goes Global (Adoption by other IPOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: CPC adoption and pilot agreements with other offices (listed: Rospatent, EPO, SIPO, KIPO, USPTO, IMPI, INPI Brazil).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPC is used for search by more than 45 Patent Offices and by more than 25,000 examiners; information on pilots and staged rollouts (e.g., KIPO, SIPO, Rospatent, INPI Brazil) should guide inter-office harmonization and training planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC Scheme (product)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPC Scheme: ~250,000 symbols organised per section (A to H and Y) and subdivided at subclass level; 1 PDF file per subclass; all XML files compressed together in a ZIP file; previous versions stored in the 'Archive' area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers/users should obtain scheme files in PDF or XML per-subclass; use archived versions to track historic classification changes. The scheme organization (sections/subclasses) informs where to place inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC Definitions (product)
rubrics_metrics.description: 626 CPC Definitions, one per subclass (around 50,000 pages of detailed CPC search and classification information). 1 PDF file per subclass; all XML files compressed together in a ZIP file. No CPC Definitions for subclasses used for indexing additional information. CPC Definitions are adapted after the revision of the corresponding part of the CPC Scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the CPC Definitions for detailed search and classification guidance for each subclass; note that some indexing-only subclasses lack Definitions and that Definitions change when the Scheme is revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC Concordances and Notices of Change (NoC)
rubrics_metrics.description: CPC Concordances (TXT, PDF, XML) mapping CPC -> IPC and CPC <-> ECLA (adapted after each CPC or IPC revision). CPC Notice of Changes (NoC) (PDF) documents detailing changes made to the scheme following a CPC Scheme revision and their impact; available one to two months prior to the entry into force of a new version of the CPC Scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concordances to map between classification systems for search and legacy data conversion; consult NoCs ahead of revisions to understand impacts and to plan reclassification or search adjustments. Note: some concordance tables are static and not updated after CPC revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC Training (e-learning and Field Specific Training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training e-learning modules provided by the EPO European Patent Academy and the USPTO; Field Specific Training (FST) for training patent examiners at patent offices classifying into CPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EPO/USPTO e-courses for baseline training; implement FST for substantive, field-specific instruction. Links provided for course access (e-courses.epo.org and USPTO CPC Training page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field Specific Training metrics and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: 476 'field specific training' sessions have been held at the EPO via video conference and recorded at the USPTO. They are being made available to the Offices classifying in the CPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded FST sessions are a resource for offices onboarding to CPC and for ongoing examiner training; track number and scope of FSTs to assess coverage across technical fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition to CPC at the USPTO (implementation timeline and effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO began the first stage of transition (~8500 examiners from USPC to CPC) in January 2014 and completed the first stage in January 2015; CPC is the classification system of record at the USPTO and all U.S. Patent Publications now carry CPC symbols. USPC collection is static (used for search as a historical collection and used for administrative workflow). USPTO will continue to classify into IPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan workflows and search strategies around CPC as the primary current classification while retaining USPC for historical searches; understand that examiner training and staged transitions were key components of implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits to USPTO and users
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits listed: US, EPO, KR, CN collections classified into one classification system for search; USPTO has one official detailed classification system for efficient search (next to IPC); CPC based on IPC puts USPTO on same footing as most of the world’s IPOs; USPTO has an up-to-date, dynamic classification system; many users worldwide using the same patent collection classified in a harmonized way for classification search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these benefits to justify CPC adoption and to guide user outreach—harmonization improves cross-office searching and consistency of prior-art retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC classification structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification hierarchy: CPC Section, Class, Subclass, Group, Subgroup (and indexing schemes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify inventions by navigating the hierarchy; be aware of both subclass-level schemes and indexing schemes that may apply for particular subject matter (e.g., enzymes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Where Biotechnology inventions are classified (high-level guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biotechnology inventions are classified across CPC Section, Class, Subclass, Group, Subgroup. Examples of CPC subclasses in TC1600 and biotechnology-related subclasses are listed (e.g., A01H, A01N, C12M, C12N, C12Q, C12R, C12Y, A61K, C07K, G01N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided list of subclasses and groups as starting points for classifying biotech inventions; multiple subclasses across A, C, G sections may be relevant depending on subject matter (plants, biocides, apparatus, microorganisms, diagnostics, medicinal preparations, peptides, antibodies, chemical analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC Subclass examples in Biotechnology (subclass definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples and brief definitions: A01H — 'New plants or processes for obtaining them; Plant reproduction by tissue culture techniques.' A01N — 'Preservation of bodies of humans, animals or plants or parts thereof; Biocides, Disinfectants including Pesticides and Herbicides.' C12M — 'Apparatus for enzymology or microbiology; Tissue, human, animal or plant cells, or virus culture apparatus.' C12N — 'Microorganisms or Enzymes; Compositions thereof; Propagating, preserving or maintaining Microorganisms; Mutation or Genetic Engineering; Culture Media, Animal Cells.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult subclass definitions for precise scope when assigning CPC symbols; the slide lists which subclass families correspond to common biotech subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC Main groups in Biotechnology (group-level examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Group-level examples: A01G33/00 — 'Cultivation of seaweed {or algae}.' A61K48/00 - A61K48/0091 — 'Medicinal preparations containing genetic material...; Gene therapy.' A61K39/00 - A61K39/70 — 'Medicinal preparations containing antigens or antibodies.' C07K14/00 - C07K14/825 — 'Peptides having more than 20 amino acids; Gastrins; Somatostatins; Melanotropins; Derivatives thereof.' C07K16/00 - C07K16/468 — 'Immunoglobulins [IGs], e.g. monoclonal or polyclonal antibodies.' G01N33/50 - G01N33/98 — 'Chemical analysis of biological material; Immunological testing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use group-level definitions to refine classification within a subclass; many biotech inventions map to these group ranges—check specific group notes for boundary and example cases (e.g., gene therapy, antibodies, peptides, diagnostics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing schemes for biotechnology (C12R, C12Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: C12R — 'Indexing scheme associated with subclasses C12N and C12Q relating to microorganisms.' C12Y — 'Enzymes — More like an indexing scheme — Created at change-over to CPC — Based on the Enzyme Commission (EC) number for classification of enzymes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying microorganisms or enzymes, apply C12R and C12Y indexing schemes to provide precise indexing (e.g., EC numbers for enzymes). Recognize that these are indexing schemes distinct from ordinary subclass/group classification and are used to add additional searchable metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major subject-matter mapping in Technology Center (TC) 1700
rubrics_metrics.description: Large mapping of CPC subclasses to subject-matter divisions for TC1700 (foodstuffs, dairy, bakery, chemical processes, polymers, coatings, microbiology, analysis, manufacturing processes, etc.), with division codes (e.g., 1790, 1740, 1730) indicating subject-matter organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the TC-to-CPC mapping to route applications to the appropriate technology group/division and to determine which examiners/divisions should handle particular CPC subclasses; the slides provide many examples across 12 pages of subject-matter areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC product formats and archival practices
rubrics_metrics.description: CPC Scheme and Definitions available in PDF and XML (one PDF per subclass; all XML files compressed in a ZIP); previous versions stored in 'Archive' area. CPC NoC (Notice of Changes) available as PDF prior to implementation of revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain official CPC files in the published formats for integration into search tools and workflows. Monitor archived versions and NoCs to maintain consistency with historical data and to implement updates when new versions enter into force.
